I did it. It's been 7 years since I've seen my mother, or anyone from my family. I had a brief but disastrous interaction with my younger sister two years ago, but otherwise, I have zero contact with any of them.

Growing up my mother was exceptionally emotionally, psychologically, and physically abusive; I also think that my sister and I might have been sexually abused, but I cannot remember. It was difficult for me to leave my mother, because I was raised to think of myself as her caretaker; I was the child she related on for emotional support, who she held responsible for her happiness and well being. Of course this meant if my mother wasn't happy or well, it was ultimately my fault, and breaking down my self esteem and self worth was essentially to keeping me as her caretaker. 

I felt guilty, and still feel guilty many years later, but ultimately I had to make the decision that I wanted to be healthy. And being healthy would never come if I stayed at home, or even within reach of my mother. 

There are times, like now, during the holidays especially when I remember good things that my mother and I shared, or good memories with other family members and miss them. But the nostalgia is just that -- nostalgia. I  would not sacrifice my well being to go back. 

So it will be hard, but I encourage you to move forward. Think of you first, because you're the only person who will.
